subject: Inference ops next steps — topology, SLOs, and agreed actions
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Marino <elena.marino@medivid.com>, Ben Hughes <ben.hughes@stratagem.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Sep 2029 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Inference ops next steps — topology, SLOs, and agreed actions

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helpful context. Below is a concise recap (call notes + technical questions / next steps) so we have an agreed starting point. I’ve attached a rough topology diagram and the sample prompts/logs you mentioned.

Summary of pain & goals (from the call)
- Primary pain: tail latency spikes and inconsistent p95 for completions — currently seeing ~1.2–1.5s p95 for 512-token responses on your hosted stack.
- Business goal: move to predictable E2E p95 of <= 300ms for short classification flows and <= 500ms for longer completions where possible; target 99th percentile below 800ms.
- Throughput: steady-state peak expected ~150–200 QPS; flash bursts up to ~350 QPS during morning surge.
- Constraints: strict data retention/compliance for PHI-ish telemetry, procurement window targeted end of Q4, and a constrained production budget for first phase.

Initial technical findings / assumptions we discussed
- Current model: medic-13B-v2 (your note) — CPU-hosted variant is likely causing high tail due to KV cache misses and lack of batching optimizations.
- Recommended primary options: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool + autoscale for bursts) OR Private VPC deployment if you need network isolation and KMS.
- Optimizations to address tail: prefix + KV caching, model quantization (q4/q4_0), sharded KV placements, continuous batching for steady-state QPS, and a small inference-compilation pass to pick best kernels for your prompt shapes.

Agreed next technical actions (proposed)
1) We’ll run a focused latency soak (lightweight canary) against a small dedicated pool using a 2hr sample of your production prompts to reproduce the p95/p99 characteristics. Deliverable: per-prompt p50/p95/p99, CPU vs GPU, cache hit-rate, and cost estimate. (Tentative window: week of 9/9)
2) You share a sanitized sample of production prompts and an anonymized set of latency logs. We’ll use these to build a KV caching profile and recommend batching settings. (I attached sample-prompts-and-latency-log.txt)
3) Security/compliance: we’ll fill the short questionnaire you asked for and surface any Private deployment gaps. Monica (cc’d) will own the SOC2/KMS questions with you.
4) Pricing: we’ll produce a two-option pricing snapshot (Dedicated vs Private) including estimated token costs and reserved capacity fees.

Open questions for you (so we can scope the canary)
- Do you have a hard requirement for p50/p95/P99 SLA or approximate budget cap for the pilot?
- Are bursts latency-sensitive (must keep p95 < X during bursts) or is graceful degradation acceptable?

Attachments: mv-inference-topology-v1.pdf, sample-prompts-and-latency-log.txt

Cheers,
Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

From: Elena Marino <elena.marino@medivid.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Hughes <ben.hughes@stratagem.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Sep 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference ops next steps — topology, SLOs, and agreed actions

Thanks Marcus — this looks right and helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Goal refinement: for short clinical classification checks we need <= 200–250ms p95 end-to-end (this is our aspiration; we understand heavy completions will be slower). For templated clinical note generation (200–600 tokens) we’d accept p95 up to 500ms.
- Throughput: our production forecast is 120–180 QPS steady state; morning surge can push to ~320 QPS for 10–15 minutes.
- Model: yes we currently run medic-13B-v2 (hosted). We’re open to trying a quantized 13B or a larger model if the economics work.

Two asks for the canary:
1) Please include a simple cost-per-hour and estimated per-million-token cost for the Dedicated and Private paths — we need this for procurement.
2) We’ll share a sanitized 2hr sample and a subset of logs (attached) — please advise on the best upload location (we prefer S3 with pre-signed link or shared drive).

Attached: sample logs (sanitized), brief compliance note.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of ML Ops, MediVid

From: Ben Hughes <ben.hughes@stratagem.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Elena Marino <elena.marino@medivid.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Sep 2029 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference ops next steps — topology, SLOs, and agreed actions

Appreciate the notes — adding a couple specifics from our side that came up in the engineering huddle: 
- Production SLOs: while the business wants aggressive p95 targets, the realistic SLO they’ll accept for full-feature rollout is p95 <= 400ms and p99 <= 900ms; anything beyond that will be flagged for escalation.
- Tail cause hypothesis: many of our tail events correlate with KV cache churn (particularly for multi-turn flows where prefix KV size grows unevenly). We need a strategy that keeps warm-entry rates high or uses sharded hot KV placement.
- Model ask: we’re evaluating moving to a medic-13B-q4 (quantized) and also want an option that supports reranking with a lightweight 1.3B model for N-best rescoring.
- Burst capacity: we need the option to burst to ~350QPS for short windows without intervention — if Dedicated can be configured with burst buffer/fallback to lower-cost instances, that’s ideal.

Procurement note: we’ve got an internal target to finalize vendor selection by 2029-12-15 — happy to prioritize a pilot.

-Ben
CTO, Stratagem.ai

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference ops next steps — topology, SLOs, and agreed actions

Looping Monica in to own the canary + compliance pieces. Monica — can you confirm availability to run a 2-hour canary during week of 9/9, and scope the test matrix? Please prepare the following by EOD 9/6 if possible:
- Test matrix: prompt buckets (short classification, mid-length completion, long completion), token counts, concurrency targets (120, 200, 320 burst), and observed metrics to capture (p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, cache hit-rate, GPU utilization).
- Baseline run plan and estimated infra cost (Dedicated vs Private).
- Short checklist for compliance items (S3 upload method, required sanitized fields, KMS key flow).

Marcus/Ben, I’ll coordinate internally for dates and get a draft pricing snapshot ready for Elena’s procurement team.

Thanks — simple and actionable.
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

[Internal note: Monica, recommend we include a short pilot addendum in the pricing doc that covers burst credits and a one-week emergency support SLA.]
